item.title: New Linux kernel fixes the long-standing scheduler stall on small boards
item.dc:creator: Jon Brodkin
item.description: The change removes a lock that kept the scheduler waiting.
item.content:encoded:
The change landed in the 6.18 merge window and removes a lock that kept the scheduler waiting under heavy I/O. Maintainers say desktop latency drops noticeably on small boards, and the patch itself is small.

What changed

Until now a task woken by a finished read had to wait for the run-queue lock even when the CPU was idle. The new code takes a lock-free path in that case:

  • wake-ups on an idle CPU no longer touch the shared lock;
  • the balancer runs less often on systems with four cores or fewer;
  • nothing changes for real-time tasks.

On a Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W the worst-case wake-up latency went from 9 ms to under 2 ms.

How to try it

  1. Build 6.18-rc2 or later.
  2. Boot with the default scheduler.
  3. Run a benchmark such as cyclictest.
cyclictest -m -p 80 -i 1000 -l 100000

The fix will be back-ported to the 6.12 long-term branch, according to the stable team. Distributions that ship 6.12 should pick it up in a few weeks. Several readers asked whether the change affects battery life on laptops; the developers expect a small gain, since an idle CPU now goes back to sleep sooner, but no measurement has been published yet.

More details are in the merge request and in the discussion on the kernel mailing list, which runs to more than two hundred messages.
